newsitem.title: USA: Conn. $500 mln bonding package delayed - report.
newsitem.headline: Conn. $500 mln bonding package delayed - report.

text.p: Democrat lawmakers intend to delay talks on the state's $500 million bonding package until Republican Gov. John Rowland is available to meet them, Hartford Courant reported Thursday.
The bonding package was supposed to have been acted on during the two- or three-day special legislative session scheduled to start on June 18.
But it appears the bonding will not be addressed until after Rowland returns from a trade mission to Israel next week, the Courant said.
The report said Rowland would not be available to meet with the Democrats until June 23 at the earliest.
The episode reflected strained relations between the governor and top Democrats, the Courant said.
Rowland on Tuesday blasted the Democrats, who control both chambers ofthe legislature, by calling the 1997 legislative session "lousy."
This year's legislative session ended on June 4.

Next week's special session is necessary to address unfinished business, including bonding, budget-implementation bills and other bills yet to be determined. Possibilities include ethics and campaign-reform bills that died awaiting action.
